hero.eyebrow: Rural Zambia · Digital skills · Remote-work readiness
hero.heading: Digital skills. A fairer start.
hero.body: Kyawama helps adults in underserved Zambian communities build practical digital skills and prepare for opportunities in remote work.
hero.visual: Approved human-centred photo, or original abstract learning path

story.heading: A personal connection. A practical beginning.
story.body: Steve Carroll's time as a Peace Corps volunteer in Zambia began a lasting connection with a host family and their community. Later, his work with Fanny Mutanda helped shape the idea behind Kyawama: make practical learning and a first professional opportunity more accessible.

person.name: Fanny Mutanda
person.body: Fanny now works as a Junior Campaign Manager at Ruvixx and brings her own experience of learning to work remotely to Kyawama's programme.

story.reviewNote: Her story predates the pilot. Do not present her as a graduate of a completed Kyawama cohort.

programme.eyebrow: Learning that connects to everyday work
programme.heading: From digital basics to professional confidence.
programme.intro: The planned programme combines classroom teaching, supervised practice and preparation for working with remote teams. Previous computer experience is not required.

stages.title: Build digital confidence
stages.body: Practise using a computer, managing email and files, creating documents and staying safe online.

stages.title: Practise working professionally
stages.body: Develop the communication, teamwork and reliable working habits that remote teams depend on.

stages.title: Prepare for opportunities
stages.body: Build a CV, prepare for interviews and learn to identify and apply for credible opportunities.

programme.expectation: Kyawama supports preparation and the search for opportunities. Completing the course does not guarantee employment.

pilot.heading: The first pilot, built around practice.
pilot.body: The weekly plan includes three two-hour lessons and a two-hour supervised practice session. The course is free for selected learners.
pilot.scheduleNote: The current plan is to begin in October 2026. The classroom venue in Zambia is being confirmed.
pilot.reviewNote: Reconfirm date, size, schedule, venue and funding dependencies before public release. Values describe plans, not completed impact.

support.heading: There is more than one way to open a door.
support.body: The pilot needs practical support, from classroom resources to people who can share their experience. Talk to us about the contribution that fits you or your organisation.

options.title: Fund the learning
options.body: Discuss support for delivery, materials, learner needs or another agreed part of the pilot.

options.title: Equip the classroom
options.body: Help with suitable computers, accessories or connectivity. Contact the team before arranging equipment.

options.title: Offer a place to learn
options.body: Explore whether a suitable classroom with power, connectivity and secure storage could support the programme.

options.title: Share experience
options.body: Contribute teaching, mentoring or practical insight into working in remote teams.

support.additional: You can also discuss credible work opportunities or help connect the team with potential learners in your community.

faq.question: Is this an online course?
faq.answer: The pilot is planned as an in-person programme in Zambia. Guest teachers may join remotely while learners work together in the classroom.

faq.question: Do learners need computer experience?
faq.answer: No previous computer experience is required. Selection includes an English comprehension assessment because lessons are delivered in English.

faq.question: Does the course guarantee a job?
faq.answer: No. It builds practical skills and professional readiness, with support in identifying and pursuing credible opportunities.

faq.question: Who should I contact?
faq.answer: Contact Steve about funding and partnerships. Contact Raeesa about programme delivery, volunteering and learner recommendations.
